newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wheatgrowers agree on AWB structure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wheatgrowers agree on AWB structure.

text.p: The Grains Council of Australia (GCA) has agreed to a new structure for the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) which involves creation of a holding company and separate subsidiaries for wheat pooling and commercial activities.

The agreement, which centres around retention of the AWB's single desk export monopoly, appears to settle a long-running debate in the Australian grains industry over the future structure of the AWB, farmer organisation officials said.

It was expected that the newly-agreed model would go to Australia's Minister for Primary Industries John Anderson for passage into legislation, a spokesman for the New South Wales Farmers' Association told Reuters.
Under the plan, A class shares in an AWB holding company will be issued to each grower at a non-transferrable nominal value.
Conversion of equity in the grower levy-funded Wheat Industry Fund to B class shares in the AWB holding company will occur in 1999.

A decision on whether the B class shares would be listed on the Australian Stock Exchange will be made following the Australian government's review of the AWB's single export desk power, Jeff Arney, GCA president, said in a statement.

Wheatgrowers who hold A class shares will elect a majority of seven directors of the holding company, with the two largest wheat-producing states of Western Australia and NSW guaranteed a minimum of two grower-elected directors.

Chairman of NSW Farmers' grains committee Xavier Martin said the new structure would be obliged to run pools every year on a non profit-making basis, returning maximum prices to growers as a priority to maximising returns to shareholders.
Re-organisation of the AWB will occur as a result of Australian government competition policy and removal of government guarantees for AWB borrowings.
GCA's agreement to the new structure removes its previous competing model, based on a trust fund arrangement, and is likely to allow AWB re-organisation to proceed, a NSW Farmers spokesman said.
This is despite continued opposition to the plan by the Western Australian Farmers Federation, the lone remaining opponent.
